title.zh: 卷一百八十一 列傳第一百三十一: 史憲誠 子孝章 何進滔 韓允忠 樂彥禎 羅弘信
title.en: Volume 181 Biographies 131: Shi Xiancheng, Zi Xiaozhang, He Jintao, Han Yunzhong, Li Yanzhen, Luo Hongxin
title.raw: 卷一百八十一 列傳第一百三十一: 史憲誠 子孝章 何進滔 韓允忠 樂彥禎 羅弘信 Volume 181 Biographies 131: Shi Xiancheng, Zi Xiaozhang, He Jintao, Han Yunzhong, Li Yanzhen, Luo Hongxin

sentences.zh: 列傳第一百三十一

translations.literal: Biographies 131
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 131

sentences.zh: 史憲誠 子孝章 何進滔 子弘敬 韓允忠 子簡 樂彥禎 子從訓 羅弘信 子威

translations.literal: Shi Xiancheng, son Xiaozhang, He Jintao, son Hongjing, Han Yunzhong, son Jian, Le Yanzhen, son Congxun, Luo Hongxin, son Wei
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xiancheng; his son Xiaozhang; He Jintao; his son Hongjing; Han Yunzhong; his son Jian; Le Yanzhen; his son Congxun; Luo Hongxin; his son Wei

sentences.zh: 史憲誠，其先出於奚虜，今為靈武建康人。

translations.literal: Shi Xiancheng: his ancestors came from the Xi barbarians; he is now a native of Jian'an in Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xiancheng was descended from the Xi people; his family was now registered at Jian'an in Lingwu.

sentences.zh: 祖道德，開府儀同三司、試太常卿、上柱國、懷澤郡王。

translations.literal: His grandfather Daode held the titles Opening the Office, Pillar of the State of the Third Order, Acting Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Supreme Pillar of the State, and Prince of Huaize Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Daode had been made Grand Preceptor of the State, Acting Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Supreme Pillar of the State, and Prince of Huaize.

sentences.zh: 父周洛，為魏博軍校，事田季安，至兵馬大使、銀青光祿大夫、檢校太子賓客、兼御史中丞、柱國、北海郡王。

translations.literal: His father Zhouluo was a WeiBo army officer serving Tian Ji'an, rising to Military Commissioner for Horse and Arms, Silver-Gleaming Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Acting Crown Prince's Guest, Concurrent Censor-in-Chief, Pillar of the State, and Prince of Beihai Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhouluo served as a WeiBo officer under Tian Ji'an and rose to command the armies, with the ranks of Silver-Gleaming Grand Master, Acting Crown Prince's Guest, Concurrent Censor-in-Chief, Pillar of the State, and Prince of Beihai.

sentences.zh: 憲誠始以材勇，隨父歷軍中右職，兼監察御史。

translations.literal: Xiancheng at first, through talent and courage, followed his father through senior posts in the army and was also made Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Xiancheng first won notice for ability and valor, followed his father through senior army posts, and was also appointed Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 元和中，田弘正討李師道，令憲誠以先鋒四千人濟河，累下其城柵。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era, Tian Hongzheng campaigned against Li Shidao and ordered Xiancheng to take four thousand vanguard troops across the river, repeatedly capturing his walled camps.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanhe reign, when Tian Hongzheng campaigned against Li Shidao, he sent Xiancheng with four thousand vanguard troops across the river; they took one fortified camp after another.

sentences.zh: 復以大軍齊進，乘勢逐北，魏之全師迫於鄆之城下。

translations.literal: Again the main army advanced together, riding the momentum in pursuit to the north; Wei's full force pressed to the walls of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: The main army then advanced in force, pressing the pursuit until the whole Wei army stood beneath the walls of Yan.

sentences.zh: 師道窮蹙，劉悟斬首投魏軍。

translations.literal: Shidao was cornered; Liu Wu beheaded him and surrendered the head to the Wei army.
translations.idiomatic: Shidao was driven to desperation; Liu Wu cut off his head and sent it to the Wei army.

sentences.zh: 錄功，超授憲誠兼中丞。

translations.literal: His merit was recorded and Xiancheng was specially promoted to Concurrent Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: His achievements were entered in the records, and Xiancheng was promoted out of turn to Concurrent Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 鎮州王承宗死，弘正自魏移領鎮州。

translations.literal: Wang Chengzong of Zhenzhou died; Hongzheng moved from Wei to take charge of Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Chengzong of Zhenzhou died, Hongzheng left Wei to take over Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 居數月，為王廷湊所殺，遂以兵叛。

translations.literal: After several months he was killed by Wang Tingcou, who then rebelled with troops.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few months he was murdered by Wang Tingcou, who then rose in armed rebellion.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以弘正子布為魏博節度使，領兵討伐，俾復父冤。

translations.literal: The court made Hongzheng's son Bu military commissioner of WeiBo, leading troops to punish the rebels and avenge his father.
translations.idiomatic: The court appointed Hongzheng's son Bu military commissioner of WeiBo and sent him to campaign against the rebels so he might avenge his father.

sentences.zh: 時幽州硃克融援助廷湊，布不能制，因自引決，軍情囂然。

translations.literal: At the time Zhu Kerong of Youzhou aided Tingcou; Bu could not control the situation and took his own life, and army sentiment grew turbulent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Kerong of Youzhou was then aiding Tingcou; Bu could not gain the upper hand and killed himself, and the army fell into uproar.

sentences.zh: 憲誠為中軍都知兵馬使，乘亂以河朔舊事動其人心，諸軍即擁而歸魏，共立為帥，國家因而命之。

translations.literal: Xiancheng was commander of the central army's horse and arms; seizing the disorder, he stirred their hearts with old Hebei stories, the armies at once rallied to Wei and jointly installed him as commander, and the state thereupon appointed him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiancheng was commander of the central army's horse and arms. He exploited the chaos, stirring the troops with old Hebei precedents; the armies at once rallied to Wei and made him their leader, and the court confirmed the appointment.

sentences.zh: 時克融、廷湊並據兵為亂，憲誠喜得旄節，雖外順朝旨，而中與硃、王為輔車之勢，長慶二年正月也。

translations.literal: At the time Kerong and Tingcou both held troops in rebellion; Xiancheng rejoiced to receive the command baton. Though outwardly he obeyed the court, inwardly he and Zhu and Wang formed a mutual-support alliance. This was in the first month of the second year of Changqing.
translations.idiomatic: Kerong and Tingcou were both in rebellion with their armies. Xiancheng was delighted to receive the commissioner's baton; though he appeared to obey the court, in secret he and Zhu and Wang were allied like paired chariots. This was in the first month of Changqing 2.

sentences.zh: 尋遣司門郎中韋文恪宣慰。

translations.literal: Soon the court sent Wei Wenke of the Department of State Affairs, Bureau of Credentials, to proclaim consolation.
translations.idiomatic: The court soon sent Wei Wenke of the Bureau of Credentials as envoy to offer reassurance.

sentences.zh: 時李㝏為亂，與憲誠書問交通。

translations.literal: At the time Li Wu was in rebellion and exchanged letters with Xiancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Wu was then in rebellion, and he and Xiancheng exchanged letters.

sentences.zh: 憲誠表請與㝏節鉞，仍於黎陽艤舟，示欲渡河。

translations.literal: Xiancheng memorialized requesting the command baton for Wu as well, and moreover moored boats at Liyang to show intent to cross the river.
translations.idiomatic: Xiancheng memorialized asking that Wu be given a commission too, and moored boats at Liyang as if preparing to cross the river.

sentences.zh: 及見文恪，舉止驕倨，其言甚悖。

translations.literal: When he met Wenke his bearing was arrogant and his words deeply defiant.
translations.idiomatic: When he met Wenke his manner was arrogant and his words openly defiant.

sentences.zh: 旋聞絺為帳下所殺，乃從改過，謂文恪曰：「憲誠蕃人，猶狗也，唯能識主。

translations.literal: Soon he heard that Wu had been killed by his own subordinates; he then changed his ways and said to Wenke: "Xiancheng is a barbarian, like a dog—he can only recognize his master.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned that Wu had been killed by his own officers, he changed his tune and told Wenke, "Xiancheng is a barbarian, no better than a dog—he knows only how to recognize his master.

sentences.zh: 雖被棒打，終不忍離。

translations.literal: Even if beaten with a stick, in the end he cannot bear to leave."
translations.idiomatic: Even if you beat him with a stick, he still cannot bring himself to leave."

sentences.zh: 」其狡譎如此。

translations.literal: His cunning and deceit were like this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the depth of his cunning.

sentences.zh: 朝廷每為優容，尋加左僕射。

translations.literal: The court repeatedly showed him forbearance and soon added the post of Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The court repeatedly indulged him, and soon promoted him to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 敬宗即位，進秩司空。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jingzong took the throne, Xiancheng was advanced to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jingzong ascended the throne, Xiancheng was promoted to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 太和二年，滄景節度使李全略卒，其子同捷竊據軍城，表邀符節，舉兵伐之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taihe, Li Quanlue, military commissioner of Cangjing, died; his son Tongjie seized the army city by stealth, memorialized requesting the command baton, and troops were raised to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 2 the Cangjing commissioner Li Quanlue died; his son Tongjie seized the garrison city and petitioned for the commission. The court raised an army against him.

sentences.zh: 先是，憲誠與全略婚媾，及同捷叛，復潛以糧餉為助。

translations.literal: Earlier Xiancheng had been allied by marriage with Quanlue; when Tongjie rebelled, he again secretly supplied grain and provisions as aid.
translations.idiomatic: Xiancheng had earlier been allied to Quanlue by marriage; when Tongjie rebelled, he again secretly sent grain and supplies.

sentences.zh: 上屢發使申諭，尋又就加平章事。

translations.literal: The emperor repeatedly sent envoys to instruct him, and soon additionally made him Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent envoys again and again to admonish him, and soon added the title Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 憲誠嘗遣驍將至闕下，恣為張大，宰相韋處厚以語折剉之，憲誠不敢復與同捷為應。

translations.literal: Xiancheng once sent fierce generals to the capital and let them boast freely; Grand Councilor Wei Chuhou rebuked them with words, and Xiancheng dared not again respond to Tongjie.
translations.idiomatic: Xiancheng once sent crack officers to the capital to swagger at will; Grand Councilor Wei Chuhou put them down in plain speech, and Xiancheng dared not aid Tongjie again.

sentences.zh: 時憲誠示出師共討同捷。

translations.literal: At the time Xiancheng made a show of taking the field to join in attacking Tongjie.
translations.idiomatic: Xiancheng then made a show of marching out to join the campaign against Tongjie.

sentences.zh: 及滄景平，加司徒。

translations.literal: When Cangjing was pacified, he was made Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: When Cangjing was pacified, he was made Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 憲誠心不自安，乃遣子孝章入覲，又飛章願以所管奉命。

translations.literal: Xiancheng's heart was not at ease; he then sent his son Xiaozhang to court and also dispatched urgent memorials offering to place his jurisdiction under command.
translations.idiomatic: Uneasy in his own mind, Xiancheng sent his son Xiaozhang to court and repeatedly memorialized that he would place his command under the throne.

sentences.zh: 上嘉之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended him for it.

sentences.zh: 乃加侍中，移鎮河中。

translations.literal: He was then made Palace Attendant and transferred to command at Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Palace Attendant and transferred to Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 憲誠素懷向背，不能以忠誠感激其眾。

translations.literal: Xiancheng had long harbored divided loyalties and could not move his troops with sincere devotion.
translations.idiomatic: Xiancheng had long been of two minds and could not win his troops with genuine loyalty.

sentences.zh: 未及出城，太和三年六月二十六日夜，為軍眾所害，冊贈太尉。

translations.literal: Before he could leave the city, on the night of the twenty-sixth day of the sixth month of the third year of Taihe, he was killed by the army masses; posthumously he was enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could even leave the city, on the night of the twenty-sixth of the sixth month, Taihe 3, the troops killed him; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 孝章，幼聰悟好學。

translations.literal: Xiaozhang in youth was clever, perceptive, and fond of learning.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhang was clever and studious from childhood.

sentences.zh: 元和中，李醞為魏帥，取大將子弟列於軍籍。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era Li Yun was Wei commander; he took sons of great generals and listed them on the military registers.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuanhe, when Li Yun commanded Wei, he enrolled the sons of senior officers on the army rolls.

sentences.zh: 孝章倡言願效文職，醞奇之，令攝府參軍。

translations.literal: Xiaozhang spoke up that he wished to serve in a civil post; Yun marveled at this and had him act as staff adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhang declared that he wished to take a civil post; Yun was impressed and appointed him acting staff adjutant.

sentences.zh: 及憲誠領節鉞，改士曹參軍、兼監察御史，賜緋。

translations.literal: When Xiancheng received the command baton, Xiaozhang was changed to Staff Officer in the Bureau of Personnel and made Concurrent Investigating Censor, with crimson robes bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiancheng received the commission, Xiaozhang became a personnel staff officer and Concurrent Investigating Censor, and was granted crimson robes.

sentences.zh: 孝章以父在鎮多違朝旨，嘗雪涕極諫，備陳逆順之理。

translations.literal: Xiaozhang, because his father in command often defied court orders, once wept as he remonstrated to the utmost, setting forth in full the principles of loyalty and rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Because his father often defied the court while in command, Xiaozhang once wept as he remonstrated with him at length on loyalty and treason.

sentences.zh: 朝廷聞而嘉之，乃授檢校太子左諭德、兼侍御史，充節度副使。

translations.literal: The court heard and commended this; he was then made Acting Left Mentor of the Crown Prince, Concurrent Attending Censor, and deputy military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When the court heard of this it commended him and appointed him Acting Left Mentor of the Crown Prince, Concurrent Attending Censor, and deputy commissioner.

sentences.zh: 累遷至散騎常侍、兼御史大夫，賜紫。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Regular Attendant at the Palace Library and Concurrent Censor-in-Chief, with purple robes bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in turn to Regular Attendant and Concurrent Censor-in-Chief, and was granted purple robes.

sentences.zh: 領本道兵同平滄景，加工部尚書。

translations.literal: He led this circuit's troops in jointly pacifying Cangjing and was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He led the circuit's troops in the pacification of Cangjing and was made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 尋請赴闕，文宗慰勞甚厚，憲誠亦因懇乞朝覲。

translations.literal: Soon he requested to go to court; Emperor Wenzong comforted and rewarded him generously, and Xiancheng also earnestly begged to attend court.
translations.idiomatic: He soon asked to go to court; Emperor Wenzong received him with warm praise, and Xiancheng also pleaded earnestly to attend in person.

sentences.zh: 上知憲誠之入覲，自孝章之謀，遂加禮部尚書，分相、衛、澶三州別為一鎮，俾孝章領之。

translations.literal: The emperor knew Xiancheng's coming to court sprang from Xiaozhang's plan; he then added Minister of Rites and separated Xiang, Wei, and Chan into a separate command for Xiaozhang to lead.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing that Xiancheng's visit was Xiaozhang's doing, the emperor made him Minister of Rites and carved Xiang, Wei, and Chan into a separate command for him to hold.

sentences.zh: 孝章未到鎮，憲誠遇害。

translations.literal: Xiaozhang had not yet reached his command when Xiancheng met with violence.
translations.idiomatic: Before Xiaozhang could reach his post, Xiancheng was killed.

sentences.zh: 上以孝章有忠節，起復為右金吾衛將軍。

translations.literal: Because Xiaozhang had shown loyal integrity, the emperor recalled him from mourning as General of the Right Gold Crow Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, honoring Xiaozhang's loyalty, recalled him from mourning as General of the Right Gold Crow Guard.

sentences.zh: 間歲，授鄜坊節度使。

translations.literal: Within a year he was made military commissioner of Bin-Fang.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was made commissioner of Bin-Fang.

sentences.zh: 居四年，遷於滑。

translations.literal: After four years he was transferred to Hua.
translations.idiomatic: After four years he was moved to Hua.

sentences.zh: 一歲，入為右領軍大將軍，改右金吾大將軍，俄授邠寧節度。

translations.literal: After one year he entered the capital as Grand General of the Right Lead Army, was changed to Grand General of the Right Gold Crow Guard, and soon received the Binning commission.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he entered the capital as Grand General of the Right Lead Army, then Grand General of the Right Gold Crow Guard, and soon received the Binning commission.

sentences.zh: 孝章歷三鎮，雖無異績，而謹身畏法，以保初終。

translations.literal: Xiaozhang held three commands; though he had no outstanding achievements, he was careful of himself and feared the law, preserving his beginning and end.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhang held three commands. He won no great distinction, but by strict self-discipline and respect for the law he kept his career intact to the end.

sentences.zh: 開成三年十月卒，贈右僕射。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the third year of Kaicheng he died; posthumously he was given Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the tenth month of Kaicheng 3 and was posthumously made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 何進滔，靈武人也。

translations.literal: He Jintao was a native of Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: He Jintao was from Lingwu.

sentences.zh: 曾祖孝物，祖俊，並本州軍校。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Xiaowu and grandfather Jun were both army officers of that prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Xiaowu and grandfather Jun had both been army officers in the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父默，夏州衙前兵馬使，檢校太子賓客，試太常卿。

translations.literal: His father Mo was horse-and-arms commissioner before the Xiazhou yamen, Acting Crown Prince's Guest, and Acting Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: His father Mo had been horse-and-arms commissioner at the Xiazhou headquarters, Acting Crown Prince's Guest, and Acting Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 以進滔之貴，贈左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Because of Jintao's eminence, Mo was posthumously given Left Regular Attendant at the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: When Jintao rose high, Mo was posthumously made Left Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 進滔客寄於魏，委質軍門，事節度使田弘正。

translations.literal: Jintao sojourned as a guest in Wei, pledged himself at the army gates, and served military commissioner Tian Hongzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Jintao had come to Wei as a guest, entered service in the army, and served under Commissioner Tian Hongzheng.

sentences.zh: 弘正奉詔討鄆州，破李師道，時進滔為衙內都知兵馬使，以功授兼侍御史。

translations.literal: Hongzheng received the edict to attack Yanzhou and defeated Li Shidao; at the time Jintao was commander of horse and arms within the headquarters and was given Concurrent Attending Censor for merit.
translations.idiomatic: When Hongzheng campaigned against Yan and defeated Li Shidao, Jintao was headquarters commander of horse and arms and was made Concurrent Attending Censor for his service.

sentences.zh: 太和三年，軍眾害史憲誠，連聲而呼曰：「得衙內都知兵馬使何端公知留後，即三軍安矣。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taihe the army masses killed Shi Xiancheng and shouted in one voice: "If we get the headquarters commander of horse and arms, Lord He of Duan, as acting commissioner, the three armies will be at peace."
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 3 the troops killed Shi Xiancheng and shouted as one: "If Lord He Duan, headquarters commander of horse and arms, becomes acting commissioner, the armies will be settled."

sentences.zh: 」推而立之。

translations.literal: They pushed him forward and installed him.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed him forward and made him their leader.

sentences.zh: 朝廷因授進滔左散騎常侍、魏博等州節度觀察處置等使。

translations.literal: The court thereupon appointed Jintao Left Regular Attendant and military commissioner for observation and disposal of WeiBo and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: The court thereupon appointed him Left Regular Attendant and military commissioner of WeiBo.

sentences.zh: 為魏帥十餘年，大得民情，累官至司徒、平章事卒。

translations.literal: As Wei commander for more than ten years he greatly won popular sentiment; he rose in office to Minister of Education and Grand Councilor and died.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded Wei for more than ten years and won deep popular regard; he rose to Minister of Education and Grand Councilor and died in office.

sentences.zh: 子弘敬襲其位。

translations.literal: His son Hongjing succeeded to his post.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hongjing succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 朝廷時遣河中帥李執方、滄州帥劉約各遣使勸令歸闕，別俟朝旨。

translations.literal: The court at times sent the Hezhong commander Li Zhifang and the Cangzhou commander Liu Yue, each dispatching envoys to urge him to return to court and await separate court orders.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent the Hezhong commander Li Zhifang and the Cangzhou commander Liu Yue, each with envoys urging him to come to court and await further orders.

sentences.zh: 弘敬不從，竟就加節制。

translations.literal: Hongjing did not obey and in the end received the full commission.
translations.idiomatic: Hongjing refused; in the end he received the full commission anyway.

sentences.zh: 及劉稹反，不時起兵。

translations.literal: When Liu Zhen rebelled, he did not raise troops in timely fashion.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Zhen rebelled, he was slow to mobilize.

sentences.zh: 鎮州王元逵下邢、洺二州，兵次上黨，弘敬方出師壓境。

translations.literal: Wang Yuankui of Zhenzhou took Xing and Ming prefectures; his troops halted at Shangdang before Hongjing at last took the field to press the border.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuankui of Zhenzhou had already taken Xing and Ming and halted at Shangdang before Hongjing finally marched out to threaten the frontier.

sentences.zh: 大中後，宣宗務其姑息，繼加官爵，亦至使相。

translations.literal: After Dazhong, Emperor Xuanzong pursued a policy of indulgence toward him, continually adding offices and titles until he too reached minister-councilor rank.
translations.idiomatic: After the Dazhong era Emperor Xuanzong indulged him with ever higher titles until he too held minister-councilor rank.

sentences.zh: 咸通初，卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiantong he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died early in the Xiantong era.

sentences.zh: 子全皞嗣之。

translations.literal: His son Quanhao succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Quanhao succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 朝廷尋降符節，累官亦至同平章事。

translations.literal: The court soon bestowed the command baton; his accumulated offices also reached Concurrent Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: The court soon granted him the commission, and his accumulated titles likewise reached Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 十一年，為軍人所害。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was killed by soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of his rule the troops killed him.

sentences.zh: 子孫相繼，四十餘年。

translations.literal: Sons and grandsons succeeded one another for more than forty years.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son had held the post in succession for more than forty years.

sentences.zh: 韓允忠，魏州人也。

translations.literal: Han Yunzhong was a native of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yunzhong was from Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 舊名君雄，懿宗改賜今名。

translations.literal: His former name was Junxiong; Emperor Yizong changed and bestowed his present name.
translations.idiomatic: He had formerly been called Junxiong; Emperor Yizong granted him his present name.

sentences.zh: 父國昌，歷本州右職。

translations.literal: His father Guochang held successive senior posts in that prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Guochang had held senior posts in the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 會昌中，從何弘敬破劉稹，以功為貝州刺史、兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the Huichang era he followed He Hongjing in defeating Liu Zhen and for merit was made prefect of Bei and Concurrent Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: During Huichang he followed He Hongjing against Liu Zhen and for his service was made prefect of Bei and Concurrent Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 以允忠故，累贈兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Because of Yunzhong, Guochang was repeatedly posthumously given Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Because of Yunzhong's rank, Guochang was repeatedly posthumously made Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 允忠少仕軍門，繼升裨校。

translations.literal: Yunzhong in youth entered service at the army gates and was promoted in succession to adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: Yunzhong entered army service young and rose through the adjutant ranks.

sentences.zh: 潞州之役，亦與其行。

translations.literal: In the Luzhou campaign he also went with the army.
translations.idiomatic: He also took part in the Luzhou campaign.

sentences.zh: 咸通十一年，何全皞為軍眾所殺，推允忠為帥。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Xiantong He Quanhao was killed by the army masses and Yunzhong was pushed forward as commander.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiantong 11 the troops killed He Quanhao and made Yunzhong their leader.

sentences.zh: 時僖宗為普王，即降詔遙領節度，授允忠左散騎常侍、兼御史中丞，充節度觀察留後。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Xizong was Prince of Pu; an edict was at once issued placing the commission under remote control, appointing Yunzhong Left Regular Attendant and Concurrent Censor-in-Chief as acting observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xizong was then still Prince of Pu; the court issued an edict placing the commission under remote appointment and made Yunzhong Left Regular Attendant and Concurrent Censor-in-Chief as acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 不數月，轉檢校工部尚書、魏州大都督府長史、充魏博節度觀察等使。

translations.literal: Within a few months he was transferred to Acting Minister of Works, Chief Administrator of the Great Capital Prefecture of Weizhou, and full WeiBo observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Within months he became Acting Minister of Works, chief administrator of Weizhou, and full WeiBo commissioner.

sentences.zh: 累加至檢校司空、同平章事。

translations.literal: He was promoted in accumulation to Acting Minister of Works and Concurrent Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in turn to Acting Minister of Works and Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 乾符元年十一月卒，年六十一。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the first year of Qianfu he died, age sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eleventh month of Qianfu 1, at the age of sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 累贈太尉。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly posthumously given Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 子簡，自允忠初授戎帥，便為節度副使。

translations.literal: His son Jian, from the time Yunzhong first received the military command, was made deputy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jian had been deputy commissioner from the moment Yunzhong took command.

sentences.zh: 乾符初，累官至檢校工部尚書。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianfu he had risen in office to Acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: By the start of Qianfu he had risen to Acting Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 允忠卒，即起復為節度觀察留後。

translations.literal: When Yunzhong died, he was at once recalled from mourning as acting observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Yunzhong died, he was recalled from mourning as acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 逾月，加檢校右僕射。

translations.literal: After more than a month he was given Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month he was made Acting Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 其後累加至侍中，封昌黎郡王。

translations.literal: Thereafter he was promoted in accumulation to Palace Attendant and enfeoffed as Prince of Changli Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to Palace Attendant and enfeoffed as Prince of Changli.

sentences.zh: 樂彥禎，魏州人也。

translations.literal: Le Yanzhen was a native of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Le Yanzhen was from Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 父少寂，歷澶、博、貝三州刺史，贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: His father Shaoji had served as prefect of Chan, Bo, and Bei and was posthumously given Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shaoji had been prefect of Chan, Bo, and Bei and was posthumously made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 彥禎少為本州軍校。

translations.literal: Yanzhen in youth was an army officer of that prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhen began as an army officer in the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 韓簡之領節旄也，以彥禎為馬步軍都虞候，轉博州刺史。

translations.literal: When Han Jian held the command baton, Yanzhen was made chief inspector of horse and foot armies and was transferred to prefect of Bo.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Jian held the commission, Yanzhen became chief inspector of the horse and foot armies and then prefect of Bo.

sentences.zh: 下河陽，走諸葛爽。

translations.literal: He took Heyang, routing Zhuge Shuang.
translations.idiomatic: He took Heyang and routed Zhuge Shuang.

sentences.zh: 有功，遷澶州刺史。

translations.literal: For merit he was moved to prefect of Chan.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was promoted to prefect of Chan.

sentences.zh: 簡再討河陽之敗也。

translations.literal: This was when Jian again campaigned against Heyang and was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: This was during Jian's second failed campaign against Heyang.

sentences.zh: 彥禎以一軍先歸，魏人遂共立之。

translations.literal: Yanzhen returned first with one army, and the people of Wei thereupon jointly installed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhen brought one army back first, and the Wei troops thereupon made him their leader.

sentences.zh: 朝廷尋授檢校工部尚書，知魏博留後。

translations.literal: The court soon appointed him Acting Minister of Works and acting WeiBo commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The court soon made him Acting Minister of Works and acting commissioner of WeiBo.

sentences.zh: 俄加戶部尚書，充節度觀察處置等使。

translations.literal: Shortly he was added Minister of Revenue and made full observation and disposal commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was also made Minister of Revenue and full military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 中和四年，累加至尚書左僕射、同平章事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhonghe he was promoted in accumulation to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Concurrent Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: By Zhonghe 4 he had risen to Left Vice Director and Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 僖宗自蜀回，加開府儀同三司，冊拜司徒。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xizong returned from Shu, Yanzhen was given Opening the Office, Pillar of the State of the Third Order, and was enfeoffed as Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xizong returned from Shu, Yanzhen was made Grand Preceptor of the State and enfeoffed as Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 彥禎志滿驕大，動多不法。

translations.literal: Yanzhen's ambitions were sated and he grew arrogant; his actions were often unlawful.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhen grew arrogant and overbearing, and his conduct was often lawless.

sentences.zh: 一旦征六州之眾，板築羅城，約河門舊堤，周八十里，月餘而畢，人用怨咨。

translations.literal: On one occasion he conscripted the masses of six prefectures to build ramparts for a walled city, following the old embankment at Hemen for a circuit of eighty li; in a little more than a month it was finished, and the people murmured in resentment.
translations.idiomatic: He once drafted labor from all six prefectures to build a new walled circuit eighty li around, following the old Hemen embankment; it was finished in little more than a month, and popular resentment ran high.

sentences.zh: 又其子從訓天資悖逆。

translations.literal: Moreover his son Congxun was by nature rebellious and perverse.
translations.idiomatic: His son Congxun, moreover, was violent and defiant by nature.

sentences.zh: 王鐸自滑移鎮滄州，過魏郊，從訓見其女妓，利之，先伏兵於漳南高雞泊，俟鐸之至，圍而害之，掠其所有。

translations.literal: Wang Duo moved from Hua to command Cangzhou and passed through Wei's outskirts; Congxun saw his female entertainers and coveted them. He first hid troops at Gaojipo south of Zhang, waited for Duo to arrive, surrounded and killed him, and plundered all he had.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Duo was transferred from Hua to Cangzhou and passed through Wei, Congxun saw his female entertainers and coveted them. He ambushed him at Gaojipo south of Zhang, killed him, and seized everything he had.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷微弱，不能詰。

translations.literal: At the time the court was weak and could not investigate.
translations.idiomatic: The court was then too weak to hold him accountable.

sentences.zh: 魏人素知鐸名望，議者惜之，而罪從訓。

translations.literal: The people of Wei had long known Duo's reputation; commentators lamented it and blamed Congxun.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Wei had long respected Duo's standing; opinion blamed Congxun and mourned the deed.

sentences.zh: 從訓又召亡命之徒五百餘輩，出入臥內，號為「子將」，委以腹心。

translations.literal: Congxun also summoned more than five hundred fugitives who came and went within his sleeping quarters, styled "son-commanders," and entrusted them with his innermost affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Congxun also gathered more than five hundred outlaws who moved freely in his private quarters, called them "son-commanders," and trusted them with his secrets.

sentences.zh: 軍人籍籍，各有異議。

translations.literal: Among the soldiers there was murmuring; each had his own opinion.
translations.idiomatic: The troops murmured among themselves, each with his own grievance.

sentences.zh: 從訓聞而忌之，易服遁出，止於近縣。

translations.literal: Congxun heard and grew jealous; he changed clothes and slipped away, stopping in a nearby county.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of this, Congxun grew wary, changed clothes, fled, and lodged in a nearby county.

sentences.zh: 彥禎因命為六州都指揮使。

translations.literal: Yanzhen thereupon appointed him overall commander of the six prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhen then appointed him overall commander of the six prefectures.

sentences.zh: 未幾，又兼相州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long he was also made concurrent prefect of Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was also made prefect of Xiang.

sentences.zh: 到任之後，般輦軍器，取索錢帛，使人來往，交午塗路，軍府疑貳。

translations.literal: After he took office he carted off military equipment and extorted money and silk; his messengers came and went until the roads were crowded, and the army headquarters grew doubtful and divided.
translations.idiomatic: Once in office he hauled away arms and extorted cash and cloth; his agents clogged the roads, and the headquarters grew uneasy and divided.

sentences.zh: 彥禎危憤而卒，眾推都將趙文㺹知留後事。

translations.literal: Yanzhen died in distress and anger; the masses pushed forward the chief commander Zhao Wenjuan to handle acting commissioner affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhen died in distress and anger; the troops made chief commander Zhao Wenjuan acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 從訓自相州領兵三萬餘人至城下，文㺹按兵不出。

translations.literal: Congxun led more than thirty thousand troops from Xiangzhou to the city walls; Wenjuan held his army and did not come out.
translations.idiomatic: Congxun marched from Xiang with more than thirty thousand men; Wenjuan kept his gates shut and would not fight.

sentences.zh: 眾懷疑懼，復害文㺹，推羅弘信為帥。

translations.literal: The masses were suspicious and afraid; they again killed Wenjuan and pushed Luo Hongxin as commander.
translations.idiomatic: The troops, uneasy and afraid, killed Wenjuan and made Luo Hongxin their leader.

sentences.zh: 弘信以兵出戰，敗之。

translations.literal: Hongxin took troops out to battle and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxin marched out and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 從訓招集餘眾，次於洹水。

translations.literal: Congxun gathered the remaining masses and encamped at Huan River.
translations.idiomatic: Congxun rallied his remnants and encamped on the Huan River.

sentences.zh: 弘信遣將程公佐領兵討擊，大敗之，梟從訓首於軍門，時文德元年春也。

translations.literal: Hongxin sent the general Cheng Gongzuo to lead troops in pursuit and attack; he inflicted a great defeat and displayed Congxun's head at the army gate. This was in the spring of the first year of Wende.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxin sent Cheng Gongzuo against him, routed him utterly, and displayed Congxun's head at the camp gate—in the spring of Wende 1.

sentences.zh: 羅弘信，字德孚，魏州貴鄉人。

translations.literal: Luo Hongxin, styled Defu, was a native of Guixiang in Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Hongxin, styled Defu, was from Guixiang in Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 曾祖秀，祖珍，父讓，皆為本州軍校。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Xiu, grandfather Zhen, and father Rang were all army officers of that prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Xiu, grandfather Zhen, and father Rang had all been army officers in the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 弘信少從戎役，歷事節度使韓簡、樂彥禎。

translations.literal: Hongxin in youth followed military service and successively served military commissioners Han Jian and Le Yanzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxin entered the army young and served under Commissioners Han Jian and Le Yanzhen.

sentences.zh: 光啟末，彥禎子從訓忌牙軍，出居於外，軍眾廢彥禎，推趙文㺹權主軍州事。

translations.literal: At the end of Guangqi, Yanzhen's son Congxun resented the牙軍, went to live outside, the army masses deposed Yanzhen, and pushed Zhao Wenjuan to provisionally manage army and prefecture affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Guangqi, Congxun, resenting the elite guard, moved outside the city; the troops deposed Yanzhen and put Zhao Wenjuan in charge.

sentences.zh: 眾復以為不便，因推弘信為帥。

translations.literal: The masses again found this unsuitable and therefore pushed Hongxin as commander.
translations.idiomatic: They soon found Wenjuan unsatisfactory and made Hongxin their leader instead.

sentences.zh: 先是，有鄰人密謂弘信曰：「某嘗夜遇一白鬚翁，相告雲，君當為土地主。

translations.literal: Earlier a neighbor had secretly told Hongxin: "I once met a white-bearded old man at night who told me you are to be lord of this land.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier a neighbor had told him in secret, "One night I met a white-bearded old man who said you would become lord of this land.

sentences.zh: 如是者再三。

translations.literal: He said so again and again."
translations.idiomatic: He said so again and again."

sentences.zh: 」弘信竊異之。

translations.literal: Hongxin privately marveled at this.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxin had privately wondered at this.

sentences.zh: 及廢文㺹，軍人聚呼曰：「孰願為節度使者？

translations.literal: When Wenjuan was deposed the soldiers gathered and shouted: "Who wishes to be military commissioner?"
translations.idiomatic: When Wenjuan was removed, the soldiers shouted together, "Who will be military commissioner?"

sentences.zh: 」弘信即應之曰：「白鬚翁早以命我。

translations.literal: Hongxin at once answered: "The white-bearded old man long ago destined me."
translations.idiomatic: Hongxin answered at once, "The white-bearded old man chose me long ago."

sentences.zh: 」眾乃環而視之，曰：「可也。

translations.literal: The masses then encircled and looked at him, saying: "He will do."
translations.idiomatic: The men surrounded him and said, "He will do."

sentences.zh: 」由是立之。

translations.literal: Thereby he was installed.
translations.idiomatic: On that basis they installed him.

sentences.zh: 僖宗聞之，文德元年四月，詔加工部尚書，權知節度留後。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xizong heard, in the fourth month of the first year of Wende an edict added Minister of Works and made him acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xizong heard, in the fourth month of Wende 1 he was made Minister of Works and acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 七月，復加金紫光祿大夫、檢校尚書右僕射，充魏博節度觀察處置等使。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he was again given Golden-Gleaming Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and made full WeiBo observation and disposal commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he was also made Golden-Gleaming Grand Master, Acting Right Vice Director, and full WeiBo commissioner.

sentences.zh: 龍紀中，加檢校司空、同平章事，封豫章郡公。

translations.literal: In Longji he was given Acting Grand Mentor of the State, Concurrent Grand Councilor, and enfeoffed as Duke of Yuzhang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: During Longji he was made Acting Grand Mentor of the State, Grand Councilor, and Duke of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 乾寧中，硃全忠急攻兗鄆，硃瑄求援於太原。

translations.literal: In Qianning, Zhu Quanzhong pressed the attack on Yan and Yun; Zhu Xuan sought aid from Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianning, Zhu Quanzhong pressed Yan and Yun hard; Zhu Xuan asked Taiyuan for help.

sentences.zh: 太原發軍，假道於魏，令大將李存信屯莘縣。

translations.literal: Taiyuan sent troops, asking passage through Wei, and ordered the great general Li Cunxin to encamp at Shen County.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan marched out, asked passage through Wei, and posted the general Li Cunxin at Shen.

sentences.zh: 存信御軍無法，侵魏之芻牧，弘信不平之。

translations.literal: Cunxin commanded the army without discipline and encroached on Wei's fodder and pastures; Hongxin was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Cunxin disciplined his men poorly and plundered Wei's fodder and pastures; Hongxin resented it.

sentences.zh: 全忠復遣人謂之曰：「太原志吞河朔，回戈之日，貴道堪憂。

translations.literal: Quanzhong again sent someone to tell him: "Taiyuan intends to swallow Hebei; on the day they turn their blades back, your honored circuit will be in peril."
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong sent word again: "Taiyuan means to swallow Hebei; when they turn homeward, your circuit will be in danger."

sentences.zh: 」弘信乃托好於汴，出師三萬攻存信，敗之。

translations.literal: Hongxin then pretended friendship with Bian, took the field with thirty thousand to attack Cunxin, and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxin then courted Bian, marched thirty thousand against Cunxin, and routed him.

sentences.zh: 太原怒，舉兵攻魏，營於觀音門外。

translations.literal: Taiyuan was enraged, raised troops to attack Wei, and encamped outside Guanyin Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan was furious, attacked Wei, and encamped outside Guanyin Gate.

sentences.zh: 汴將葛從周援之，屯於洹水。

translations.literal: The Bian general Ge Congzhou came to aid him and encamped at Huan River.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Congzhou of Bian came to his aid and encamped on the Huan.

sentences.zh: 李克用子落落時為鐵林軍使，為從周所擒，乃退歸。

translations.literal: Li Keyong's son Luoluo was then commander of the Iron Forest Army; he was captured by Congzhou, and they then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong's son Luoluo, then commander of the Iron Forest Army, was captured by Congzhou, and Taiyuan withdrew.

sentences.zh: 自是太原之師，每歲侵擾相、魏，魏人患之。

translations.literal: From this time Taiyuan's armies each year raided Xiang and Wei, and the people of Wei suffered from it.
translations.idiomatic: After that Taiyuan raided Xiang and Wei every year, to Wei's great distress.

sentences.zh: 硃全忠方事兗鄆，懼弘信離貳，每歲時賂遺，必卑辭厚禮答貺。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong was then engaged with Yan and Yun and feared Hongxin might turn aside; every year at the seasons he sent gifts, always answering return gifts with humble words and lavish courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong was then busy with Yan and Yun and feared Hongxin might turn away; every season he sent gifts, and always returned courtesies with humble words and lavish presents.

sentences.zh: 全忠對魏使北面拜而受之，曰：「六兄比予倍年已上，兄弟之國，安得以常鄰遇之。

translations.literal: Quanzhong faced north and bowed to receive Wei envoys, saying: "Sixth Elder Brother is more than twice my years; as brother states, how can we be treated as ordinary neighbors?"
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong bowed northward to receive Wei's envoys and said, "Sixth Elder Brother is more than twice my age; as brother states, how can we treat each other as ordinary neighbors?"

sentences.zh: 」弘信以為厚己，亦推心焉。

translations.literal: Hongxin thought himself richly honored and also gave his heart in trust.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxin took this as deep regard for himself and gave Quanzhong his trust in return.

sentences.zh: 弘信累官至檢校太師、守侍中、臨清王。

translations.literal: Hongxin rose in office to Acting Grand Preceptor, Guardian Palace Attendant, and Prince of Linqing.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxin rose to Acting Grand Preceptor, Guardian Palace Attendant, and Prince of Linqing.

sentences.zh: 光化元年九月卒，年六十三，贈太師，追封北平王，謚曰莊肅。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the first year of Guanghua he died, age sixty-three; posthumously he was given Grand Preceptor, posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Northern Peace, posthumous title Zhuangsu.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the ninth month of Guanghua 1, at sixty-three; he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor, enfeoffed as Prince of Northern Peace, and given the posthumous title Zhuangsu.

sentences.zh: 子威。

translations.literal: His son Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Wei.

sentences.zh: 威，字端己。

translations.literal: Wei, styled Duanji.
translations.idiomatic: Wei, styled Duanji.

sentences.zh: 文德初，授左散騎常侍，充天雄軍節度副使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wende he was given Left Regular Attendant and made deputy commissioner of the Tianxiong Army.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Wende he was made Left Regular Attendant and deputy commissioner of the Tianxiong Army.

sentences.zh: 自龍紀至乾寧，十年之中，累加官爵。

translations.literal: From Longji to Qianning, within ten years he was repeatedly given offices and titles.
translations.idiomatic: From Longji through Qianning, over ten years, his titles rose steadily.

sentences.zh: 弘信卒，襲父位為留後，朝廷從而命之。

translations.literal: When Hongxin died, he succeeded his father's post as acting commissioner, and the court followed by appointing him.
translations.idiomatic: When Hongxin died, Wei succeeded him as acting commissioner, and the court confirmed the appointment.

sentences.zh: 天復末，累加至檢校太傅、兼侍中、長沙王。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianfu he was promoted in accumulation to Acting Grand Tutor, Concurrent Palace Attendant, and Prince of Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of Tianfu he had risen to Acting Grand Tutor, Palace Attendant, and Prince of Changsha.

sentences.zh: 天祐初，授檢校太尉、守侍中，進封鄴王，賜號「忠勤宣力致理功臣」。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianyou he was given Acting Grand Commandant, Guardian Palace Attendant, advanced to Prince of Ye, and granted the epithet "Meritorious Minister of Loyal Diligence, Proclaiming Power, and Ordering the Realm."
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianyou he was made Acting Grand Commandant and Guardian Palace Attendant, advanced to Prince of Ye, and granted the epithet Loyal and Diligent Minister Who Proclaims Power and Orders the Realm.

sentences.zh: 魏之牙中軍者，自至德中，田承嗣盜據相、魏、澶、博、衛、貝等六州，召募軍中子弟置之部下，遂以為號。

translations.literal: Wei's 牙中軍: from the Zhide era Tian Chengsi seized by stealth Xiang, Wei, Chan, Bo, Wei, and Bei and the other six prefectures, recruited sons of army families and placed them under his command, and thus they took this name.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's elite guard corps dated from the Zhide era, when Tian Chengsi seized the six prefectures of Xiang, Wei, Chan, Bo, Wei, and Bei and enrolled soldiers' sons in his own units—hence the name.

sentences.zh: 皆豐給厚賜，不勝驕寵。

translations.literal: All were richly supplied and lavishly rewarded, beyond bearing in pride and favor.
translations.idiomatic: They were richly paid and lavishly rewarded, and grew insufferably arrogant.

sentences.zh: 年代浸遠，父子相襲，親黨膠固。

translations.literal: As years gradually lengthened, father and son succeeded one another and kin cliques bonded solid.
translations.idiomatic: Over the generations fathers and sons succeeded one another, and kin networks grew as tight as glue.

sentences.zh: 其凶戾者，強買豪奪，逾法犯令，長吏不能禁。

translations.literal: The violent among them forced purchases and seized by might, transgressing law and violating orders; senior officials could not restrain them.
translations.idiomatic: The worst among them extorted and seized by force, breaking every law; their superiors could not stop them.

sentences.zh: 變易主帥，有同兒戲，如史憲誠、何進滔、韓君雄、樂彥禎，皆為其所立。

translations.literal: Changing commanders was like child's play; such men as Shi Xiancheng, He Jintao, Han Junxiong, and Le Yanzhen were all installed by them.
translations.idiomatic: Replacing commanders was child's play; Shi Xiancheng, He Jintao, Han Junxiong, and Le Yanzhen had all been installed by them.

sentences.zh: 優獎小不如意，則舉族被害。

translations.literal: If rewards and favors fell slightly short of satisfaction, whole clans were destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: If rewards fell even slightly short, whole families were slaughtered.

sentences.zh: 威懲其往弊，雖以貨賂姑息，而心銜之。

translations.literal: Wei punished their past abuses; though he placated them with goods and bribes, in his heart he harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Wei meant to end their abuses; though he bought them off with gifts, he nursed a grudge in his heart.

sentences.zh: 威嗣世之明年，正月，幽州劉仁恭擁兵十萬，謀亂河朔，進陷貝州，長驅攻魏。

translations.literal: In the year after Wei succeeded to the post, in the first month, Liu Rengong of Youzhou massed a hundred thousand troops, plotted disorder in Hebei, advanced and took Bei Prefecture, and drove at full speed to attack Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the year after Wei succeeded his father, Liu Rengong of Youzhou marched a hundred thousand men to stir trouble in Hebei, took Bei, and drove straight at Wei.

sentences.zh: 威求援於汴。

translations.literal: Wei sought aid from Bian.
translations.idiomatic: Wei asked Bian for help.

sentences.zh: 硃全忠遣將李思安屯於洹水。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong sent the general Li Si'an to encamp at Huan River.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong sent Li Si'an to encamp on the Huan.

sentences.zh: 葛從周自邢、洺引軍入魏。

translations.literal: Ge Congzhou led troops from Xing and Ming into Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Congzhou brought his army in from Xing and Ming.

sentences.zh: 燕將劉守文、單可及攻汴軍於內黃。

translations.literal: The Yan generals Liu Shouwen and Shan Keji attacked Bian troops at Neihuang.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan generals Liu Shouwen and Shan Keji attacked the Bian army at Neihuang.

sentences.zh: 思安逆戰，大敗之，乘勝追躡。

translations.literal: Si'an met them in battle and inflicted a great defeat, riding victory in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Si'an met them and routed them, then pressed the pursuit.

sentences.zh: 從周出會掩擊，覆敗燕軍，斬首三萬。

translations.literal: Congzhou came out to join in a concealed strike and utterly defeated the Yan army, beheading thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Congzhou joined the fight with a flanking strike and shattered the Yan army, taking thirty thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 三年，威引汴軍攻滄州以報之。

translations.literal: In the third year Wei led Bian troops to attack Cangzhou in reprisal.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Wei led Bian's army against Cangzhou in reprisal.

sentences.zh: 自是，威感全忠援助之恩，合從景附。

translations.literal: From this time Wei felt gratitude for Quanzhong's aid and joined in alliance, following his lead.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Wei was grateful for Quanzhong's help and clung to his alliance.

sentences.zh: 天祐二年七月十三日夜，牙軍裨校李公佺作亂，威僅以身免。

translations.literal: On the night of the thirteenth day of the seventh month of the second year of Tianyou, the elite guard adjutant Li Gongxian mutinied, and Wei barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of the thirteenth of the seventh month, Tianyou 2, adjutant Li Gongxian of the elite guard mutinied, and Wei barely escaped alive.

sentences.zh: 公佺出奔滄州。

translations.literal: Gongxian fled to Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gongxian fled to Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 自是愈懼，遣使求援於全忠，密謀破之。

translations.literal: From this he grew ever more afraid, sent envoys to seek aid from Quanzhong, and secretly plotted to destroy them.
translations.idiomatic: He grew more afraid than ever, sent to Quanzhong for aid, and secretly plotted their destruction.

sentences.zh: 全忠遣李思安會魏博軍，再攻滄州。

translations.literal: Quanzhong sent Li Si'an to join WeiBo troops in again attacking Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong sent Li Si'an with the WeiBo army to attack Cangzhou again.

sentences.zh: 全忠女妻威子廷規，先是卒。

translations.literal: Quanzhong's daughter had married Wei's son Tinggui; she had died earlier.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong's daughter had married Wei's son Tinggui; she had died some time before.

sentences.zh: 全忠遣長直軍校馬嗣勳選兵千人，密於輿中實兵甲入魏，言助女葬事。

translations.literal: Quanzhong sent the long-service guard officer Ma Sixun to select a thousand troops, secretly filling palanquins with armor and weapons to enter Wei, saying they came to assist with the daughter's funeral.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong sent guard officer Ma Sixun with a thousand picked men, arms hidden in funeral carts, on the pretext of helping bury his daughter.

sentences.zh: 三年正月五日，嗣勳至，全忠親率大軍濟河，言視行營於滄景。

translations.literal: On the fifth day of the first month of the third year Sixun arrived; Quanzhong personally led a great army across the river, saying he was going to inspect the camps at Cangjing.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth of the first month, Tianyou 3, Sixun arrived; Quanzhong himself crossed the river with a great army, saying he would inspect the Cangjing front.

sentences.zh: 威欲因而出迎，至期，即假全忠帳下銳卒入而夾攻之。

translations.literal: Wei wished to take the occasion to go out to welcome him; when the day came, he would borrow Quanzhong's crack troops from the headquarters to enter and strike them from both sides.
translations.idiomatic: Wei planned to go out to welcome him and, when the day came, use Quanzhong's crack troops inside the city to attack the guard from both sides.

sentences.zh: 牙軍頗疑，堅請不出。

translations.literal: The elite guard was quite suspicious and firmly begged him not to go out.
translations.idiomatic: The elite guard grew suspicious and insisted he stay inside.

sentences.zh: 威恐洩其事，慰納之。

translations.literal: Wei feared the affair would leak and comforted and appeased them.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing his plot would leak, Wei soothed and reassured them.

sentences.zh: 是月十四日夜，率廝養百十輩，與嗣勳合攻之。

translations.literal: On the night of the fourteenth day of that month he led a hundred-odd personal attendants and joined Sixun in attacking them.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of the fourteenth he led a hundred-odd personal retainers and joined Sixun in the attack.

sentences.zh: 時宿於牙城者千人，遲明殺之殆盡；

translations.literal: At the time a thousand lodged in the牙城; by late dawn they were killed nearly to the last man;
translations.idiomatic: A thousand of the guard were quartered in the headquarters city; by dawn nearly all were dead;

sentences.zh: 凡八千家，皆破其族。

translations.literal: eight thousand households in all had their clans destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: eight thousand households in all had their entire clans wiped out.

sentences.zh: 魏軍攻滄州者，在歷亭聞有變，其將史仁遇擁之，保於高唐。

translations.literal: The Wei troops attacking Cangzhou, at Liting, heard there was a disturbance; their general Shi Renyu rallied them and held fast at Gaotang.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei troops besieging Cangzhou, encamped at Liting, heard of the upheaval; their commander Shi Renyu rallied them and held Gaotang.

sentences.zh: 六州之內，皆為讎敵，累月平之。

translations.literal: Within the six prefectures all became enemies; it took months to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the six prefectures every survivor was treated as an enemy; it took months to pacify the region.

sentences.zh: 威仕梁數年後卒，年三十四，位至守太師、兼中書令，贈尚書令，謚曰貞壯。

translations.literal: After serving Liang for several years Wei died, age thirty-four; he had reached Guardian Grand Preceptor and Concurrent Director of the Secretariat, was posthumously given Director of the Department of State Affairs, posthumous title Zhenzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: After several years in Liang's service Wei died at thirty-four, having reached Guardian Grand Preceptor and Concurrent Director of the Secretariat; he was posthumously made Director of the Department of State Affairs with the posthumous title Zhenzhuang.

sentences.zh: 威性明敏，達於吏道。

translations.literal: Wei's nature was bright and keen; he was accomplished in the ways of administration.
translations.idiomatic: Wei was quick and perceptive and skilled in administration.

sentences.zh: 伏膺儒術，招納文人，聚書至萬卷。

translations.literal: He devoted himself to Confucian learning, gathered literati, and amassed books to ten thousand scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted himself to the classics, gathered scholars, and built a library of ten thousand scrolls.

sentences.zh: 每花朝月夕，與賓佐賦詠，甚有情致。

translations.literal: On every flower-season morning and moonlit evening he composed and chanted poetry with guests and staff, with much feeling and charm.
translations.idiomatic: On spring mornings and moonlit evenings he would compose poetry with his staff, with real grace and feeling.

sentences.zh: 錢塘人羅隱者，有當世詩名，自號「江東生」。

translations.literal: Luo Yin of Qiantang had contemporary fame in poetry and styled himself "Born east of the River."
translations.idiomatic: Luo Yin of Qiantang enjoyed great poetic fame in his day and styled himself Born East of the River.

sentences.zh: 威遣使賂遺，敘其宗姓，推為叔父。

translations.literal: Wei sent envoys with gifts, set forth their shared clan name, and honored him as uncle.
translations.idiomatic: Wei sent gifts, claimed kinship through a shared clan name, and honored him as uncle.

sentences.zh: 隱亦集其詩寄之。

translations.literal: Yin also gathered his poems and sent them to him.
translations.idiomatic: Yin in turn sent him a collection of his poems.

sentences.zh: 威酷嗜其作，目己所為曰《偷江東集》，凡五卷，今鄴中人士諷詠之。

translations.literal: Wei was passionately fond of his works and titled his own compositions Collected Plunderings from East of the River, five scrolls in all; today people in Ye recite and chant them.
translations.idiomatic: Wei adored his work, titled his own poems Collected Plunderings from East of the River in five scrolls, and they are still recited in Ye.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：魏、鎮、燕三鎮，不能制之也久矣。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Wei, Zhen, and Yan—the three commands—the court has long been unable to control them.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: The court has long been unable to control the three commands of Wei, Zhen, and Yan.

sentences.zh: 兵強地廣，合從連衡。

translations.literal: Their armies are strong and their lands broad; they ally in vertical and horizontal leagues.
translations.idiomatic: Their armies are strong, their territories vast, and they league together in shifting alliances.

sentences.zh: 爵命雖假於朝廷，群臣自謀於元帥。

translations.literal: Though titles and appointments are borrowed from the court, the ministers plot among themselves under their commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Though titles come from the court on loan, the ministers plot under their own commanders.

sentences.zh: 如史憲誠等五家，其初皆因此而得之，其後亦因此而失之。

translations.literal: Such five houses as Shi Xiancheng's at first all gained their posts through this means, and later also lost them through this means.
translations.idiomatic: The five houses represented by Shi Xiancheng first won their commands in this way, and later lost them in the same way.

sentences.zh: 蓋不知取之以權，守之以仁，則遠矣。

translations.literal: For they did not know to take power through expedient means and hold it through benevolence—then they would have been far from ruin.
translations.idiomatic: They did not understand how to seize power by expedient means and keep it through benevolence; that path was far beyond them.

sentences.zh: 若善繼者，史氏、羅氏之二子有焉，其餘不足觀也。

translations.literal: If one speaks of those who succeeded well, the two sons of the Shi and Luo houses had this quality; the rest are not worth regarding.
translations.idiomatic: Among those who carried the line forward worthily, only the two sons of the Shi and Luo houses qualify; the rest are hardly worth notice.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：逆取順守，古亦有之。

translations.literal: The encomium says: To take the realm in rebellion and hold it in obedience—antiquity too had such cases.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium reads: Seizing power by force yet ruling thereafter in accord with the throne—history offers precedents even for that.

sentences.zh: 如其逆守，滅亡必隨。

translations.literal: If one holds power in the manner of rebellion, destruction and extinction surely follow.
translations.idiomatic: But if one holds power in the spirit of rebellion, ruin is sure to follow.

sentences.zh: 史、何、韓、樂，世數盛衰。

translations.literal: Shi, He, Han, and Le—generation after generation rose and fell.
translations.idiomatic: The houses of Shi, He, Han, and Le rose and fell across the generations.

sentences.zh: 足以為鑒，念茲在茲。

translations.literal: They are sufficient to serve as a mirror; let this be kept firmly in mind.
translations.idiomatic: They are warning enough; let the lesson be kept always in mind.
